extracted.intended_audience: scholars and practitioners of natural philosophy; readers/students of Bacon and history/philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance (Baconian) for conducting, presenting, and organizing natural-philosophical inquiry: how to use experiment and reason, what motives and procedures are proper, and the intended structure of a comprehensive Instauratio of the sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the work / Instauratio
rubrics_metrics.description: To effect a restoration (Instauratio) of the sciences so that the commerce between Mind and Things is retrieved and human doctrine is founded on proper grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work aims to give a principle and beginning to a project that may be continued by others: 'Ut vero errores ... ipsi se corrigerent ... Restabat illud unum ut res de integro tentetur melioribus praesidiis, utque fiat ... Instauratio.' The end is practical improvement of sciences rather than mere speculative contestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of experience and experiment over pure dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy must rely principally on experience and experiments rather than on dialectical subtleties or abstract reasoning divorced from phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialectic 'ad civilia ... rectissime adhibeatur' but fails to reach nature's subtlety; it 'ad errores potius stabilendos' apt. The author proposes an 'Interpretatione Naturae' — an art akin to logic but grounded in experimental aids so intellect may be 'exaltetur' and 'amplificetur ad naturae ardua et obscura superanda.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility of the intellect in inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should practice humility: refrain from assuming the mind's unaided authority, avoid fanciful invocations of own spirit as oracle, and keep intellect close to things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast earlier inventors who 'quasi inventio nil aliud esset quam quaedam excogitatio' with the proposed chastity: 'inter res caste et perpetuo versantes, intellectum longius a rebus non abstrahimus.' Humility is required both in discovering and in teaching: 'quam In inveniendo adhibemus humilitatem, eandem et in docendo sequuti sumus.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper motives for scientific work
rubrics_metrics.description: Science should be pursued for the use and benefit of life, the glory of God, and human good — not for fame, power, contention, or vanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admonition: 'nec eam aut animi causa petant, aut ad contentionem, aut ut alios despiciant, aut ad commodum, aut ad famam, aut ad potentiam' but 'ad meritum et usus vitae; eamque in charitate perficiant et regant.' The ethical aim moderates ambition and pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderliness and avoidance of premature abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry and experimentation must proceed in ordered steps from simpler, sensory-near phenomena to remoter, hidden aspects; avoid hasty generalizations and premature abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy to divine order: do not expect all at once ('primo die lucem tantum creavit... sequentibus diebus ad ea descendit'). 'Omnisque via, usque a primis ipsis sensuum perceptionibus, certa ratione munienda' — vestigia filo regenda sunt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments with definite aims and avoid erratic trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments must be purposeful and planned to be fruitful rather than 'erraticam inquisitionem' or 'pussilla' aims that produce trivial results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of mechanical experimenters who set 'pusilla quaedam pensa' for large claims; recommend 'fructifera (inquam) experimenta, non lucifera' and warn against 'opera praepropero et intempestivo studio captavit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjoin empirical and rational faculties (legitimate conjunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formally marry empirical observation and rational analysis so that neither empiricism nor pure reasoning dominates improperly; produce a 'conjugium verum et legitimum'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project 'firmasse' a 'conjugium verum et legitimum' between empiric and rational faculties which have been 'morosa et inauspicata divortia et repudia.' The method aims to reconcile and employ both in continuous methodical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, openness, and plain presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Present discoveries and doctrines 'aperte et perspicue' — nakedness of mind and simplicity aid reception; exposition should be plain, not obscure or deliberately authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author states 'Pars autem instituti nostri est, ut omnia, quantum fieri potest, aperte et perspicue proponantur.' Avoid confounding readers by mere display of erudition or by 'obscuritatis velo'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward authority and consensual longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept the long-standing consensus or authoritative statements as proof of truth; evaluate by usefulness, experiment, and close inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning that consensus and time are fallible: 'neque ipse consensus atque diuturnitas magni prorsus aestimandus est.' 'Neque illud afferat quispiam, scientias paullatim succrescentes tandem ad statum quendam pervenisse' — do not equate duration with correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making science an ornament; favor growth and practical improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sciences should progress and produce operative results like mechanical arts rather than remain static, ornamental, or merely disputational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast philosophy and intellectual sciences (which are 'adorantur et celebrantur, sed non promoventur') with mechanical arts that 'quotidie crescunt et perficiuntur.' Aim for 'incrementa' and usable advances rather than rhetorical triumphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and substantive treatment of neglected topics
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing omitted or due divisions and topics, supply more than light titles — include substantive argument or exemplar so readers can grasp the intended work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any omitted subject is returned ('siquid inter omissa retulerimus') and is obscure, provide parts of the work or examples so the reader is not left with a 'levem notionem' of the project; avoid mere headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition and structural plan of the work (six parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall program is to be divided into six parts: Partitiones Scientiarum; Novum Organum (Indicia for interpretation of Nature); Historia Naturalis et Experimentalis to found philosophy; Scala Intellectus; Prodromi (Anticipations of the Second Philosophy); and Philosophia Secunda (Active Science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Distribution is explicit: 'Ejus constituuntur Partes sex. Prima: Partitiones Scientiarum. Secunda: Novum Organum... Sexta: Philosophia Secunda, sive Scientia Activa.' Each part has a specified role (e.g., first: summary/description of existing sciences; second: doctrine for better use of reason; third: natural history and experiments to build philosophy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use senses appropriately (sensus) and do not separate natural inquiry from them
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ senses as the foundation for inquiry (senses open the terrestrial globe as the sun), and do not treat natural investigation as if it were interdicted from sense use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admonition: 'Monemus primum ... ut homines sensum in officio, quoad divina, contineant.' But likewise 'ne hujusce mali fuga in contrarium peccent ... si naturae inquisitionem ulla ex parte veluti interdicto separant.' Sensory perception must be the first step, properly ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and charity in scientific disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists should avoid excess, arrogance, and moral dangers of knowledge; pursue science 'in charitate' and with regard to human limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral warnings: 'Postulata ... ne humana divinis officiant ... quod ne... aliquid incredulitatis ... oboriatur.' Also: 'Ex appetitu scientiae, homines; sed charitatis non est excessus; neque angelus aut homo per eam umquam in periculum venit.'
